subject.title: fix(cron): pass allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent from cron executor for both runner paths

question: Should OpenClaw treat clean empty assistant replies as silent success for all cron jobs by passing `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` unconditionally at the cron executor boundary, or should that behavior be narrowed to no-deliver/per-job policy?
rationale: The patch is a clean owner-boundary fix, but it intentionally changes cron result and delivery semantics for existing announce/webhook jobs, which is a product compatibility decision rather than an automation-repair decision.

options.title: Accept all-cron silent success
options.body: Approve this PR as the canonical fix if empty cron output should mean nothing to report for no-deliver, announce, and webhook cron jobs.

options.title: Narrow before merge
options.body: Require the branch to gate the flag on delivery mode or a per-job option if empty output should remain an error for some delivery-requested jobs.

options.title: Pause the cron policy change
options.body: Leave the PRs open or close them as not planned if maintainers do not want to change the current empty-response signal.

recommendation.title: Accept all-cron silent success
recommendation.body: Approve this PR as the canonical fix if empty cron output should mean nothing to report for no-deliver, announce, and webhook cron jobs.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied to both the empty-response merge path and recent adjacent silent/live inference behavior, making him the best routing owner from the available history.
